title: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus: Recognition, Isolation and Escalation
specialty: Infectious Diseases / Respiratory Medicine / Emergency Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus: Recognition, Isolation and Escalation
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: The current Saudi MERS case definition and isolation duration require live verification at each presentation.
No disease-specific antiviral dose was verified.

pathophysiology.summary: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus infects the respiratory tract and can cause viral pneumonia. Severe disease can progress to acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure and multiorgan dysfunction. Healthcare transmission requires immediate infection-prevention controls.
keyMechanisms: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus infects the respiratory tract and can cause viral pneumonia.
Severe disease can progress to acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure and multiorgan dysfunction.
Healthcare transmission requires immediate infection-prevention controls.

symptoms: Fever, cough, breathlessness and gastrointestinal symptoms may occur.
physicalSigns: Hypoxaemia, tachypnoea, focal or diffuse chest signs and systemic illness.
redFlags: Escalating oxygen requirement, shock, altered consciousness or organ dysfunction.
precipitants: Recent healthcare exposure, close contact with a confirmed case, or epidemiological exposure defined by current Saudi public-health criteria.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Focal bacterial source or culture evidence; coinfection remains possible.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Current Saudi case-definition exposure or contact
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Isolate and notify infection prevention/public health without waiting for laboratory confirmation.

clinicalManagement.title: Isolate and notify
actions: Place the patient in the locally designated isolation pathway; use current airborne/contact precautions for aerosol-generating procedures.
Notify infection prevention and the Saudi public-health pathway immediately.

clinicalManagement.title: Support organ function
actions: Titrate oxygen and ventilatory support to physiology; manage sepsis and shock using the local critical-care protocol.
Investigate and treat bacterial coinfection when clinically suspected.

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate and trace
actions: Refer early to critical care for increasing oxygen needs or organ dysfunction.
Support public-health contact identification and testing instructions.

medicationPlan.note: No routine MERS-specific antiviral regimen is included. Provide supportive care and use the current Saudi MOH/Weqaya and hospital antimicrobial protocol for proven or suspected coinfection.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Apply the current Saudi MOH/Weqaya case definition; criteria change and must be checked at presentation.

teaching.scope: Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus: Recognition, Isolation and Escalation
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Escalating oxygen requirement, shock, altered consciousness or organ dysfunction.
